strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with In-Place Scaling
strategies.desc: Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches with in-place element-wise scaling operations between stages. Each all-reduce operates on the full (world*256,) tensor, with scaling/unscaling applied locally via loops over shards. This is the baseline approach with 8 AR dispatches and minimal memory overhead but maximum compute overhead from repeated scaling loops.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-Reduce with Precomputed Coefficients
strategies.desc: Precomputes all scale/unscale coefficient combinations into lookup tables, then fuses adjacent scale+clone operations into single vectorized operations before each all-reduce. Reduces local compute overhead through vectorization and eliminates redundant clone operations where possible, maintaining 8 AR dispatches but with reduced host overhead.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing per-rank ownership of shards during intermediate stages. Uses 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but enables potential pipelining and reduces memory bandwidth since each rank only needs to scale its owned shard between RS and AG phases.

strategies.name: Batched All-Reduce with Metadata Views
strategies.desc: Reorganizes data into a (8, world*256) tensor where dimension 0 represents stages, applies all scaling transformations as tensor views/reshapes, then dispatches all 8 all-reduces together if framework supports batched collectives. Trades memory (8x buffer) for potential dispatch coalescing and better hardware utilization.

strategies.name: Ring-Based Cumulative Scaling Pipeline
strategies.desc:
Implements custom ring algorithm where each stage's scaled data is sent point-to-point in a pipelined fashion, accumulating results progressively. Uses O(world) send/recv pairs per stage instead of all-reduce, potentially hiding latency through pipelining but with higher dispatch count (8*world point-to-point ops) suitable only if per-dispatch overhead is negligible.
